title: Stories of Sages Mandakarani and Agastya
introduction: Rama comes across lake from which divine music is heard. Surprised at the musical notes from beneath the waters of the lake he enquires with the sage who is following, and that sage narrates the episode of Sage Mandakarni. Then Rama proceeds on wondering at that lake, and he visits all the hermitages about there and thus elapsed are ten years. Again Rama returns to the hermitage of Sage Suteekhsna, and after staying there for some time, takes leave of that sage and proceeds to see Sage Agastya. And on the way he visits the brother of Sage Agastya also. Rama, on the way narrates about the great deeds done by Sage Agastya in protecting humans from demons, and also depicts the propitious nature of Agastya's hermitage.
closing: इति वाल्मीकि रामायणे आदि काव्ये अरण्य काण्डे एकादशः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 11th chapter in Aranya Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
अग्रतः प्रययौ रामः सीता मध्ये सुशोभना |
पृष्ठतः तु धनुष्पाणिः लक्ष्मणः अनुजगाम ह
verses.iast:
agrataḥ prayayau rāmaḥ sītā madhye suśobhanā |
pṛṣṭhataḥ tu dhanuṣpāṇiḥ lakṣmaṇaḥ anujagāma ha
verses.translation: Rama travelled ahead while the glorious Seetha in middle, and wielding bow Lakshmana followed them on the rear.
notes: This verse is commented specially by the ancient narrators. It is said that Om, praNava is reflected in this verse. The Om is the compound of three letters a + u + ma, and the first letter in the verse is a , in a + grataH. The second letter of Om, i.e., u is u in su sobhanā. Other versions may read this as su madhyamā , even then this u is there. The letter before last word ha is ma , as in jagā ma . These three letters put together are Om. So the three, Rama, Lakshmana, Seetha are compared with these three letters of Om.

Vishnu/Rama is in letter a and he is coursing ahead, agrartaḥ prayayau , followed by u, Lakshmi/Seetha, who is an embodiment of the Absolute's karuṇa , benevolence, as said at lakśmyā kāruṇya rūpayā And she is the illusory aspect of that Absolute, Maya, yāmā ye mï¿½ , and being so, she will be the veil in between that Absolute and Innate Soul. The last letter ma is makāro jīva vācaka, makāro dāsa vācaka, is the sign for the servitude of the Innate Soul to the Absolute. That is what Lakshmana is.

And anu jagāma means that which follows without any I-ness or Mine-ness as a total surrender, kainkarya . This agrataḥ prayayau rāmaḥ is said to be the leadership quality of Soul, or Rama, where he does it himself without preaching, like Krishna. Previously when they entered forests, Lakshmana was leading and showing the way, as a dutiful servant. During next phase all three walked in line. Now, Rama wanted to wage war with demons, thus he leads the way, keeping Seetha in centre, followed and guarded by Lakshmana. This is the view point of the sages following them, for they the sages always meditate about that Absolute, in terms of Om, and these three appeared as the three letters of Om.

glosses.meaning: Seetha, in middle, very, glorious one
rear, lakSmaNaH Lakshmana, but, bow, wielding

verses.devanagari:
तौ पश्यमानौ विविधान् शैल प्रस्थान् वनानि च |
नदीः च विविधा रम्या जग्मतुः सह सीतया
verses.iast:
tau paśyamānau vividhān śaila prasthān vanāni ca |
nadīḥ ca vividhā ramyā jagmatuḥ saha sītayā
verses.translation: They proceeded while seeing diverse mountain terraces, forests, and diversely enchanting rivers too, along with Seetha.

verses.devanagari:
सारसान् चक्रवाकां च नदी पुलिन चारिणः |
सरांसि च सपद्मानि युतानि जलजैः खगैः
verses.iast:
sārasān cakravākāṃ ca nadī pulina cāriṇaḥ |
sarāṃsi ca sapadmāni yutāni jalajaiḥ khagaiḥ
verses.translation: Beholding the rivers that have water-birds like saarasa, chakravaaka that move on their sandbanks, and also the lakes that contain lotuses and water born birds, they moved on.

verses.devanagari:
यूथ बद्धाम् च पृषतान् मद उन्मत्तान् विषाणिनः |
महिषाम् च वराहाम् च गजाम् च द्रुम वैरिणः
verses.iast:
yūtha baddhām ca pṛṣatān mada unmattān viṣāṇinaḥ |
mahiṣām ca varāhām ca gajām ca druma vairiṇaḥ
verses.translation: The moved on watching spotted deer banded in herds, the wild boars, large horned buffaloes maddened in virility, and the ruttish elephants rending trees like their enemies.

glosses.meaning: elephants, too, that are trees', animals.

verses.devanagari:
ते गत्वा दूरम् अध्वानम् लंबमाने दिवाकरे |
ददृशुः सहिता रंयम् तटाकम् योजन आयुतम्
पद्म पुष्कर संबाधम् गज यूथैः अलंकृतम् |
सारसैः हंस कादम्बैः संकुलम् जल जातिभिः
verses.iast:
te gatvā dūram adhvānam lambamāne divākare |
dadṛśuḥ sahitā raṃyam taṭākam yojana āyutam
padma puṣkara sambādham gaja yūthaiḥ alaṅkṛtam |
sārasaiḥ haṃsa kādambaiḥ saṅkulam jala jātibhiḥ
verses.translation: On going far on their way, and when the sun is dangling in the western skiy, together they saw a charming lake of one yojana width fully overloaded with red and white lotuses, overspread with sporting elephants, and over-flurried with waterfowls like saarasa birds, kaadamba birds, swans and with others kinds too.

glosses.meaning: together, they, far way, on way, having gone
while dangling, sun [sun while hanging in western sky]
with red lotuses, white lotuses, fully, overloaded
sarasa birds, swans, kaadamba water-fowls, flurried

verses.devanagari:
प्रसन्न सलिले रम्ये तस्मिन् सरसि शुश्रुवे |
गीत वादित्र निर्घोषो न तु कश्चन दृश्यते
verses.iast:
prasanna salile ramye tasmin sarasi śuśruve |
gīta vāditra nirghoṣo na tu kaścana dṛśyate
verses.translation: Out of the tranquil and enchanting waters of that lake audible are the melodies of singing and musical instruments, but none is visible.

verses.devanagari:
ततः कौतूहलात् रामो लक्ष्मणः च महारथः |
मुनिम् धर्मभृतम् नाम प्रष्टुम् समुपचक्रमे
verses.iast:
tataḥ kautūhalāt rāmo lakṣmaṇaḥ ca mahārathaḥ |
munim dharmabhṛtam nāma praṣṭum samupacakrame
verses.translation: Then Rama and also Lakshmana, the great charioteer, inquisitively started to ask the Sage named Dharmabhrita about it.

verses.devanagari:
इदम् अत्यद्भुतम् श्रुत्वा सर्वेषाम् नो महामुने |
कौतूहलम् महत् जातम् किम् इदम् साधु कथ्यताम्
verses.iast:
idam atyadbhutam śrutvā sarveṣām no mahāmune |
kautūhalam mahat jātam kim idam sādhu kathyatām
verses.translation: "On hearing this greatly amazing music from lake, oh, great saint, intensive inquisitiveness is created in all of us, why this, please tell us clearly about it." Thus Rama asked.

verses.devanagari:
तेन एवम् उक्तो धर्मात्मा राघवेण मुनिः तदा |
प्रभावम् सरसः क्षिप्रम् आख्यातुम् उपचक्रमे
verses.iast:
tena evam ukto dharmātmā rāghaveṇa muniḥ tadā |
prabhāvam sarasaḥ kśipram ākhyātum upacakrame
verses.translation: Thus said by that Raghava then that virtuous sage quickly started to tell about the efficacy of that lake.

glosses.meaning: then, by him, by Raghava, thus, said

verses.devanagari:
इदम् पंच अप्सरो नाम तटाकम् सार्व कालिकम् |
निर्मितम् तपसा राम मुनिना माण्डकर्णिना
verses.iast:
idam paṃca apsaro nāma taṭākam sārva kālikam |
nirmitam tapasā rāma muninā māṇḍakarṇinā
verses.translation: "Oh, Rama, this is an all-time lake built by the ascetic power of the sage Mandakarni, known as Five Apsara Lake.

glosses.meaning: this one is, five apsara, named, lake.

verses.devanagari:
स हि तेपे तपः तीव्रम् माण्डकर्णिः महामुनिः |
दश वर्ष सहस्राणि वायु भक्षो जलाशये
verses.iast:
sa hi tepe tapaḥ tīvram māṇḍakarṇiḥ mahāmuniḥ |
daśa varṣa sahasrāṇi vāyu bhakṣo jalāśaye
verses.translation: "He that great saint Mandakarni practiced rigorous ascesis for ten thousand years staying in the waters of the lake, and consuming air alone.

verses.devanagari:
ततः प्रव्यथिताः सर्वे देवाः स अग्नि पुरोगमाः |
अब्रुवन् वचनम् सर्वे परस्पर समागताः
verses.iast:
tataḥ pravyathitāḥ sarve devāḥ sa agni purogamāḥ |
abruvan vacanam sarve paraspara samāgatāḥ
verses.translation: "Then all the gods are worried and met together with Fire-god at the helm of affairs, and they all conversed among themselves.

glosses.meaning: with, Fire, at helm of affairs

verses.devanagari:
अस्मकम् कस्यचित् स्थानम् एष प्रार्थयते मुनिः |
इति संविग्न मनसः सर्वे तत्र दिवौकसः
verses.iast:
asmakam kasyacit sthānam eṣa prārthayate muniḥ |
iti saṃvigna manasaḥ sarve tatra divaukasaḥ
verses.translation: "This sage is praying for someone's place among us," thus all of those heaven-dwellers are perturbed at heart.

glosses.meaning: among us, someone's, place, he is praying for
all, heaven-dwellers, in that matter, are perturbed, at heart.

verses.devanagari:
ततः कर्तुम् तपो विघ्नम् सर्व देवैः नियोजिताः |
प्रधान अप्सरसः पंच विद्युत् चलित वर्चसः
verses.iast:
tataḥ kartum tapo vighnam sarva devaiḥ niyojitāḥ |
pradhāna apsarasaḥ paṃca vidyut calita varcasaḥ
verses.translation: "Then all gods assigned five important Apsara-s, the celestial courtesans, whose shine is like the sprint of the lightning, to effectuate hindrance in that sage's ascesis.

verses.devanagari:
अप्सरोभिः ततः ताभिः मुनिः दृष्ट परावरः |
नीतो मदन वश्यत्वम् देवानाम् कार्य सिद्धये
verses.iast:
apsarobhiḥ tataḥ tābhiḥ muniḥ dṛṣṭa parāvaraḥ |
nīto madana vaśyatvam devānām kārya siddhaye
verses.translation: Then those five celestial beauties have led that sage astray who discerned the nature of this and the other world, or good and bad, or the nature of Absolute-Soul and Body- bound Soul, towards the passional restraint by, as though to achieve god's task.

glosses.meaning: sage, who discerned, other, and this world [knows worldly and heavenly matters,] sage
by them, by five of the celestials

verses.devanagari:
ताः चैव अप्सरसः पंच मुनेः पत्नीत्वम् आगताः |
तटाके निर्मितम् तासाम् तस्मिन् अन्तर्हितम् गृहम्
verses.iast:
tāḥ caiva apsarasaḥ paṃca muneḥ patnītvam āgatāḥ |
taṭāke nirmitam tāsām tasmin antarhitam gṛham
verses.translation: "Also thus, those five celestial apsara-s attained wifehood of that sage, and for them he built a house in there, concealed inside that lake.

glosses.meaning: they, also thus, five of them, celestials
in there, in lake, inside concealed, is built.

verses.devanagari:
तत्र एव अप्सरसः पंच निवसन्त्यो यथा सुखम् |
रमयन्ति तपोयोगात् मुनिम् यौवनम् आस्थितम्
verses.iast:
tatra eva apsarasaḥ paṃca nivasantyo yathā sukham |
ramayanti tapoyogāt munim yauvanam āsthitam
verses.translation: "While those five celestial apsara-s are living in there, they are gratifying that sage according to his delight as youthfulness came upon that sage owing to his power of asceticism.

glosses.meaning: there, alone, apsara-s, five of them
as for, his delight, they are gratifying.

verses.devanagari:
तासाम् संक्रीड मानानाम् एष वादित्र निःस्वनः |
श्रूयते भूषण उन्मिश्रः गीत शब्दः मनोहरः
verses.iast:
tāsām saṅkrīḍa mānānām eṣa vāditra niḥsvanaḥ |
śrūyate bhūṣaṇa unmiśraḥ gīta śabdaḥ manoharaḥ
verses.translation: "These musical sounds we hear are emerging out as played on their instruments, mingled with the tinkling of their ornaments, and mixed with their delightful singing of melodies." So said sage Dharmabhrita to Rama.

glosses.meaning: their, playing instruments, sounds they are
delightful, singing, of melodies, being heard.

verses.devanagari:
आश्चर्यम् इति तस्य एतद् वचनम् भावितात्मनः |
राघवः प्रतिजग्राह सह भ्रात्रा महा यशाः
verses.iast:
āścaryam iti tasya etad vacanam bhāvitātmanaḥ |
rāghavaḥ pratijagrāha saha bhrātrā mahā yaśāḥ
verses.translation: That highly renowned Raghava together with his brother acknowledged the sage Dharmabhrita's account, exclaiming it as "amazing is this..."

verses.label: 3.11.21, 22a
verses.devanagari:
एवम् कथयमानः स ददर्श आश्रम मण्डलम् |
कुश चीर परिक्षिप्तम् ब्राह्म्या लक्ष्म्या समावृतम्
प्रविश्य सह वैदेह्या लक्ष्मणेन च राघवः |
verses.iast:
evam kathayamānaḥ sa dadarśa āśrama maṇḍalam |
kuśa cīra parikṣiptam brāhmyā lakśmyā samāvṛtam
praviśya saha vaidehyā lakṣmaṇena ca rāghavaḥ |
verses.translation: While saying thus Raghava has seen a cluster of hermitages nearby, encircled with sacred grass, jute cloths, and even encompassed with Vedic solemness, and he entered that hermitage along with Seetha and Lakshmana.

glosses.meaning: sacred grass, jute cloths, encircled with

verses.label: 3.11.22b, 23, 24a
verses.devanagari:
तदा तस्मिन् स काकुत्स्थः श्रीमति आश्रम मण्डले
उषित्वा स सुखम् तत्र पूर्ज्यमानो महर्षिभिः |
जगाम च आश्रमान् तेषाम् पर्यायेण तपस्विनाम् |
येषाम् उषितवान् पूर्वम् सकाशे स महास्त्रवित् |
verses.iast:
tadā tasmin sa kākutsthaḥ śrīmati āśrama maṇḍale
uṣitvā sa sukham tatra pūrjyamāno maharṣibhiḥ |
jagāma ca āśramān teṣām paryāyeṇa tapasvinām |
yeṣām uṣitavān pūrvam sakāśe sa mahāstravit |
verses.translation: Rama happily stayed in that august cluster of hermitages duly venerated by those great saints for sometime, and then that expert in great missiles Rama went to the hermitages of those sages with whom he stayed earlier, for another round.

glosses.meaning: then, in that august, hermitage's, cluster of
earlier, with whom, in nearness, he resided

verses.label: 3.11.24b, 25, 26a
verses.devanagari:
क्वचित् परिदशान् मासान् एक संवत्सरम् क्वचित्
क्वचित् च चतुरो मासान् पंच षट् च परान् क्वचित् |
अपरत्र अधिकान् मासान् अध्यर्धम् अधिकम् क्वचित्
त्रीन् मासान् अष्ट मासान् च राघवो न्यवसत् सुखम् |
verses.iast:
kvacit paridaśān māsān eka saṃvatsaram kvacit
kvacit ca caturo māsān paṃca ṣaṭ ca parān kvacit |
aparatra adhikān māsān adhyardham adhikam kvacit
trīn māsān aṣṭa māsān ca rāghavo nyavasat sukham |
verses.translation: Rama stayed there for nearly ten months at some place, elsewhere for one year, at somewhere else for four months, and for five, and six months at elsewhere, even at somewhere else for more than a month, and for more than one and half months elsewhere.

glosses.meaning: at some place, also, four months
more than month, much time, somewhere else
one and half, more than, three, months

verses.label: 3.11.26b, 27a
verses.devanagari:
तत्र संवसतः तस्य मुनीनाम् आश्रमेषु वै
रमतः च आनुकूल्येन ययुः संवत्सरा दश |
verses.iast:
tatra saṃvasataḥ tasya munīnām āśrameṣu vai
ramataḥ ca ānukūlyena yayuḥ saṃvatsarā daśa |
verses.translation: While Raghava stayed comfortably taking delight in those hermitages of sages, indeed ten years have smoothly elapsed.
notes: As per the above the counof monthst comes to sixty months, i.e., five years. But it is said that ten years are elapsed comfortably. There are a good number of arguments counting the months said above and the point of ten years, said finally. Dharmaakuutam puts it as ten years only: tataḥ paryāyeṇa nikhila muni jana nilayeṣu nītvā daśa samvatsarān punarāgamya tīkṣṇatapasaḥ sutīkṣṇam || Thus ten full years are spent only in around these hermitages, peregrinating from one to the other. The total period of exile is fourteen years. Here it is said that ten years are completed. In Chitrakuta two years are spent. Then the search for Seetha and final war should happen in two year span.

glosses.meaning: of them, the sages, hermitages, indeed

verses.label: 3.11.27b, 28a
verses.devanagari:
परिसृत्य च धर्मज्ञः राघवः सह सीतया
सुतीक्ष्णस्य आश्रमम् श्रीमान् पुनर् एव आजगाम ह |
verses.iast:
parisṛtya ca dharmajñaḥ rāghavaḥ saha sītayā
sutīkṣṇasya āśramam śrīmān punar eva ājagāma ha |
verses.translation: Thus that virtue-knowing glorious Rama on going around those hermitages along with Seetha indeed went to the hermitage of Sage Suteekshna again.

glosses.meaning: along with, Seetha, on going around
to sage Suteekshna's, hermitage, went to, indeed.

verses.label: 3.11.28b, 29a
verses.devanagari:
स तम् आश्रमम् आगम्य मुनिभिः परिपूजितः
तत्र अपि न्यवसत् रामः कंचित् कालम् अरिन्दमः |
verses.iast:
sa tam āśramam āgamya munibhiḥ paripūjitaḥ
tatra api nyavasat rāmaḥ kañcit kālam arindamaḥ |
verses.translation: On coming at that hermitage that enemy destroyer is adored by sages, and he resided there for some time.

glosses.meaning: there, even, for some time, resided.

verses.label: 3.11.29b, 30a
verses.devanagari:
अथ आश्रमस्थो विनयात् कदाचित् तम् महामुनिम्
उपासीनः स काकुत्स्थः सुतीक्ष्णम् इदम् अब्रवीत् |
verses.iast:
atha āśramastho vinayāt kadācit tam mahāmunim
upāsīnaḥ sa kākutsthaḥ sutīkṣṇam idam abravīt |
verses.translation: Then on one day while staying in that hermitage Rama submissively said this to that sage Suteekshna who is sitting nearby.

glosses.meaning: then, in hermitage, while staying, Rama
to that, great, saint, to Suteekshna, who is sitting nearby.

verses.label: 3.11.30b, 31a
verses.devanagari:
अस्मिन् अरण्ये भगवन् अगस्त्यो मुनिसत्तमः
वसति इति मया नित्यम् कथाः कथयताम् श्रुतम् |
verses.iast:
asmin araṇye bhagavan agastyo munisattamaḥ
vasati iti mayā nityam kathāḥ kathayatām śrutam |
verses.translation: "I have always heard through the narratives narrated by other sages that the godly and eminent sage Agastya is residing in this forest.

glosses.meaning: in this, forest, lives, thus as

verses.label: 3.11.31b, 32a
verses.devanagari:
न तु जानामि तम् देशम् वनस्य अस्य महत्तया
कुत्र आश्रम पदम् पुण्यम् महर्षेः तस्य धीमतः |
verses.iast:
na tu jānāmi tam deśam vanasya asya mahattayā
kutra āśrama padam puṇyam maharṣeḥ tasya dhīmataḥ |
verses.translation: "But due to the vastness of this forest I have not known that place, where is the pious hermitage of that astute sage?

glosses.meaning: that astute one's, of that, sage

verses.label: 3.11.32b, 33a
verses.devanagari:
प्रसाद अर्थम् भगवतः सानुजः सह सीतया
अगस्त्यम् अभिगच्छ्हेयम् अभिवादयितुम् मुनिम् |
verses.iast:
prasāda artham bhagavataḥ sānujaḥ saha sītayā
agastyam abhigacchheyam abhivādayitum munim |
verses.translation: "I wish to approach that sage seeking that godly sage's graciousness, along with my brother and Seetha to venerate him.

glosses.meaning: graciousness, desiring, of that godly sage
that sage, to Agastya, to venerate, I wish to approach.

verses.label: 3.11.33b, 34a
verses.devanagari:
मनोरथो महान् एष हृदि परिवर्तते
यदि अहम् तम् मुनिवरम् शुश्रूषेयम् अपि स्वयम् |
verses.iast:
manoratho mahān eṣa hṛdi parivartate
yadi aham tam munivaram śuśrūṣeyam api svayam |
verses.translation: "Can I personally propitiate that supreme sage -- is my high ambition, and it is recurrent in my heart." So said Rama to Suteekshna.

glosses.meaning: in my, heart, it is recurring.

verses.label: 3.11.34b, 35a
verses.devanagari:
इति रामस्य स मुनिः श्रुत्वा धर्मात्मनो वचः
सुतीक्ष्णः प्रत्युवाच इदम् प्रीतो दशरथात्मजम् |
verses.iast:
iti rāmasya sa muniḥ śrutvā dharmātmano vacaḥ
sutīkṣṇaḥ pratyuvāca idam prīto daśarathātmajam |
verses.translation: Sage Suteekshna on hearing that particular request of that virtue-minded Rama is gladdened and said this to him.

glosses.meaning: this kind of, words [that particular request of Rama,] on hearing

verses.label: 3.11.35b, 36b
verses.devanagari:
अहम् अपि एतद् एव त्वाम् वक्तु कामः स लक्ष्मणम्
अगस्त्यम् अभिगच्छ्ह इति सीतया सह राघव |
verses.iast:
aham api etad eva tvām vaktu kāmaḥ sa lakṣmaṇam
agastyam abhigacchha iti sītayā saha rāghava |
verses.translation: "Oh, Raghava, even I wished to say this to you, that you may approach Agastya along with Lakshmana and Seetha.

glosses.meaning: to you, with Lakshmana, with Seetha

verses.label: 3.11.36b, 37a
verses.devanagari:
दिष्ट्या तु इदानीम् अर्थे अस्मिन् स्वयम् एव ब्रवीषि माम्
अयम् आख्यामि ते राम यत्र अगस्त्यो महामुनिः |
verses.iast:
diṣṭyā tu idānīm arthe asmin svayam eva bravīṣi mām
ayam ākhyāmi te rāma yatra agastyo mahāmuniḥ |
verses.translation: "But providentially you alone raised this topic with me, Rama, I will tell you where that great sage Agastya is.

glosses.meaning: yourself, alone, to me, you are speaking
= where, Agastya, great sage is there

verses.label: 3.11.37b
verses.devanagari:
योजनानि आश्रमात् तात याहि चत्वारि वै ततः |
दक्षिणेन महान् श्रीमान् अगस्त्य भ्रातुर् आश्रमः
verses.iast:
yojanāni āśramāt tāta yāhi catvāri vai tataḥ |
dakṣiṇena mahān śrīmān agastya bhrātur āśramaḥ
verses.translation: "On your going four yojana-s from this hermitage, oh, dear Rama, there is the great and glorious hermitage of Agastya's brother on the southern side. [4-11-37b, c]

glosses.itrans: tataH dakSiNena agastya bhraatuH mahaan shriimaan aashramaH
glosses.iast: tataḥ dakṣiṇena agastya bhrātuḥ mahān śrīmān āśramaḥ
glosses.devanagari: ततः दक्षिणेन अगस्त्य भ्रातुः महान् श्रीमान् आश्रमः
glosses.meaning: then on west side, Agastya, brother's, great, glorious, hermitage [is there.]

verses.devanagari:
स्थली प्राय वनोद्देशे पिप्पली वन शोभिते |
बहु पुष्प फले रम्ये नाना विहग नादिते
verses.iast:
sthalī prāya vanoddeśe pippalī vana śobhite |
bahu puṣpa phale ramye nānā vihaga nādite
verses.translation: "That hermitage is there on a plateau in a spectacular place of that forest which is adorned with many flowers and fruits, thickets of long pepper, and reechoed with the callings of various birds.

glosses.meaning: pippali = with trees [long pepper,] thickets, adorned with
in forest, place [that hermitage is there.]

verses.label: 3.11.39, 40a
verses.devanagari:
पद्मिन्यो विविधाः तत्र प्रसन्न सलिल आशयाः |
हंस कारण्डव आकीर्णाः चक्रवाक उपशोभिताः
तत्र एकाम् रजनीम् व्युष्य प्रभाते राम गम्यताम् |
verses.iast:
padminyo vividhāḥ tatra prasanna salila āśayāḥ |
haṃsa kāraṇḍava ākīrṇāḥ cakravāka upaśobhitāḥ
tatra ekām rajanīm vyuṣya prabhāte rāma gamyatām |
verses.translation: "There are diverse lakes that are receptacles for tranquil waters, that are teeming with swans and partridges, beautified with ruddy geese, and Rama staying there for a night you may proceed in the next morning.

glosses.meaning: with swans, francolin partridges, teeming with

verses.label: 3.11.40b, 41a
verses.devanagari:
दक्षिणाम् दिशम् आस्थाय वन षण्डस्य पार्श्वतः
तत्र अगस्त्य आश्रम पदम् गत्वा योजनम् अन्तरम् |
verses.iast:
dakṣiṇām diśam āsthāya vana ṣaṇḍasya pārśvataḥ
tatra agastya āśrama padam gatvā yojanam antaram |
verses.translation: "On going one yojana beyond, taking the southward course on the side of the forest clump you will find Agastya's hermitage.

glosses.meaning: one yojana, afterward - beyond, on going

verses.label: 3.11.41b, 42
verses.devanagari:
रमणीये वनोद्देशे बहु पादप शोभिते
रंस्यते तत्र वैदेही लक्ष्मणः च त्वया सह |
स हि रम्यो वनौद्देशो बहु पादप संयुतः
verses.iast:
ramaṇīye vanoddeśe bahu pādapa śobhite
raṃsyate tatra vaidehī lakṣmaṇaḥ ca tvayā saha |
sa hi ramyo vanauddeśo bahu pādapa saṃyutaḥ
verses.translation: "Seetha and Lakshmana will enjoy those woodlands adorned with diverse pleasant trees, as the woodlands abounding with diverse trees will naturally be delightful, isn't it.

glosses.meaning: pleasant, with divers, trees, adorned with

glosses.itrans: tatra vanoddeshe vaidehii lakSmaNaH ca tvayaa saha ramsyate
glosses.iast: tatra vanoddeśe vaidehī lakṣmaṇaḥ ca tvayā saha ramsyate
glosses.devanagari: तत्र वनोद्देशे वैदेही लक्ष्मणः च त्वया सह रम्स्यते
glosses.meaning: in that, woodlands, Vaidehi, Lakshmana, also, you, along with, will enjoy
that, woodland, is delightful, isn't it.

verses.devanagari:
यदि बुद्धिः कृता द्रष्टुम् अगस्त्यम् तम् महामुनिम् |
अद्य एव गमने बुद्धिम् रोचयस्व महामते
verses.iast:
yadi buddhiḥ kṛtā draṣṭum agastyam tam mahāmunim |
adya eva gamane buddhim rocayasva mahāmate
verses.translation: "If your mind is made up to see that great sage Agastya, oh, great ingenious Rama, resolve your thinking in going only today." So said Sage Suteekshna to Rama.

glosses.meaning: to see, Agastya, that, great sage

verses.devanagari:
इति रामो मुनेः श्रुत्वा सह भ्रात्रा अभिवाद्य च |
प्रतस्थे अगस्त्यम् उद्दिश्य सानुगः सह सीतया
verses.iast:
iti rāmo muneḥ śrutvā saha bhrātrā abhivādya ca |
pratasthe agastyam uddiśya sānugaḥ saha sītayā
verses.translation: On listening that which is said by the sage, Rama revered that sage along with his brother, and then he journeyed with Seetha and his follower Lakshmana aiming to reach Agastya.

glosses.meaning: of sage, that is said, on listening

verses.devanagari:
पश्यन् वनानि चित्राणि पर्वतां च अभ्र संनिभान् |
सरांसि सरितः चैव पथि मार्ग वश अनुगतान्
सुतीक्ष्णेन उपदिष्टेन गत्वा तेन पथा सुखम् |
इदम् परम संहृष्टो वाक्यम् लक्ष्मणम् अब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
paśyan vanāni citrāṇi parvatāṃ ca abhra saṃnibhān |
sarāṃsi saritaḥ caiva pathi mārga vaśa anugatān
sutīkṣṇena upadiṣṭena gatvā tena pathā sukham |
idam parama saṃhṛṣṭo vākyam lakṣmaṇam abravīt
verses.translation: While viewing beautiful forests, cloud-like mountains, lakes, and rivers that are flowing following the pathways, Rama happily journeyed on the pathway indicated by sage Suteekshna, then he gladly spoke this sentence to Lakshmana.

glosses.meaning: walkway, along, following -- that are flowing

verses.devanagari:
एतद् एव आश्रम पदम् नूनम् तस्य महात्मनः |
अगस्त्यस्य मुनेर् भ्रातुर् दृश्यते पुण्य कर्मणः
verses.iast:
etad eva āśrama padam nūnam tasya mahātmanaḥ |
agastyasya muner bhrātur dṛśyate puṇya karmaṇaḥ
verses.translation: "Definitely this alone appears to be the hermitage of Sage Agastya's brother, one with great soul and pious deeds.

glosses.meaning: of great souled one, with pious deeds

verses.devanagari:
यथा हि इमे वनस्य अस्य ज्ञाताः पथि सहस्रशः |
संनताः फल भरेण पुष्प भारेण च द्रुमाः
verses.iast:
yathā hi ime vanasya asya jñātāḥ pathi sahasraśaḥ |
saṃnatāḥ phala bhareṇa puṣpa bhāreṇa ca drumāḥ
verses.translation: "As how thousands of trees are bowing under the weight of flowers and fruit on the pathway, thereby I perceive it to be the hermitage of Agastya's bother.

glosses.itrans: pathi phala bhareNa puSpa bhaareNa ca
glosses.iast: pathi phala bhareṇa puṣpa bhāreṇa ca
glosses.devanagari: पथि फल भरेण पुष्प भारेण च
glosses.meaning: on way, by fruit's, weight, by flower's, weight, too

verses.devanagari:
पिप्पलीनाम् च पक्वानाम् वनाद् अस्माद् उपागतः |
गन्धो अयम् पवन उत्क्षिप्तः सहसा कटुकोदयः
verses.iast:
pippalīnām ca pakvānām vanād asmād upāgataḥ |
gandho ayam pavana utkṣiptaḥ sahasā kaṭukodayaḥ
verses.translation: "Upraised by the wind the sour-smell of pippali fruits is suddenly coming closer from the forest.

verses.devanagari:
तत्र तत्र च दृश्यन्ते संक्षिप्ताः काष्ठ संचयाः |
लूनाः च परिदृश्यन्ते दर्भा वैदूर्य वर्चसः
verses.iast:
tatra tatra ca dṛśyante saṅkṣiptāḥ kāṣṭha sañcayāḥ |
lūnāḥ ca paridṛśyante darbhā vaidūrya varcasaḥ
verses.translation: "Here and there visible are the well heaped heaps of firewood, and all over appearing is the sacred grass snipped at its top and gemlike in its tinge.

verses.devanagari:
एतत् च वन मध्यस्थम् कृष्ण अभ्र शिखर उपमम् |
पावकस्य आश्रमस्थस्य धूमाग्रम् संप्रदृश्यते
verses.iast:
etat ca vana madhyastham kṛṣṇa abhra śikhara upamam |
pāvakasya āśramasthasya dhūmāgram sampradṛśyate
verses.translation: "From inside the hermitage in the midst of this forest the vertex of smoke from ritual fire is clearly visible as high as the vertex of a black rainy cloud.

verses.devanagari:
विविक्तेषु च तीर्थेषु कृत स्नाना द्विजातयः |
पुष्प उपहारम् कुर्वन्ति कुसुमैः स्वयम् आर्जितैः
verses.iast:
vivikteṣu ca tīrtheṣu kṛta snānā dvijātayaḥ |
puṣpa upahāram kurvanti kusumaiḥ svayam ārjitaiḥ
verses.translation: "On performing bathing in sacred streams the Brahmans are making flower offerings to gods, called puSpa bali, with the flowers that are personally collected by them.
notes: If flowers for worship are taken from someone else, half of the merit of that worship goes to the one who gave those flowers. Hence the flowers are to be plucked by the worshipper alone, that too from his flower garden. They are not to be stolen, begged, carried in palms, or in upper cloth, but to be carried in a big size leaf.
"Best are the flowers brought personally, medium is the forest-born, purchased are the worse, and those that are brought by others, the worst."

verses.devanagari:
ततः सुतीक्ष्णस्य वचनम् यथा सौम्य मया श्रुतम् |
अगस्त्यस्य आश्रमो भ्रातुर् नूनम् एष भविष्यति
verses.iast:
tataḥ sutīkṣṇasya vacanam yathā saumya mayā śrutam |
agastyasya āśramo bhrātur nūnam eṣa bhaviṣyati
verses.translation: "Thus by the words of Sage Suteekshna as I have heard, oh, gentle Lakshmana, this hermitage shall definitely be that of Sage Agastya's brother.

verses.devanagari:
निगृह्य तरसा मृत्युम् लोकानाम् हित काम्यया |
यस्य भ्रात्रा कृता इयम् दिक् शरण्या पुण्य कर्मणा
verses.iast:
nigṛhya tarasā mṛtyum lokānām hita kāmyayā |
yasya bhrātrā kṛtā iyam dik śaraṇyā puṇya karmaṇā
verses.translation: "Whose brother is Sage Agastya with meritorious deeds, who wishing well-being of the world controlled death by his efficacy, and who made this southern region a liveable region, this must be the hermitage of such a sage, such Agatya's brother.

verses.devanagari:
इह एकदा किल क्रूरो वातापिः अपि च इल्वलः |
भ्रातरौ सहितौ आस्ताम् ब्राह्मणघ्नौ महा असुरौ
verses.iast:
iha ekadā kila krūro vātāpiḥ api ca ilvalaḥ |
bhrātarau sahitau āstām brāhmaṇaghnau mahā asurau
verses.translation: "Once upon a time verily cruel demon brothers Vaataapi and Ilvala were here together, and they the dreadful demons, they say, used to be Bhraman-killers.

glosses.meaning: cruel ones, Vaataapi, even, also, Ilvala

glosses.itrans: bhraatarau mahaa asurau sahitau aastaam kila
glosses.iast: bhrātarau mahā asurau sahitau āstām kila
glosses.devanagari: भ्रातरौ महा असुरौ सहितौ आस्तां किल
glosses.meaning: brothers, dreadful demons, together, they were here, they say.

verses.devanagari:
धारयन् ब्राह्मणम् रूपम् इल्वलः संस्कृतम् वदन् |
आमंत्रयति विप्रान् स श्राद्धम् उद्दिश्य निर्घृणः
verses.iast:
dhārayan brāhmaṇam rūpam ilvalaḥ saṃskṛtam vadan |
āmaṃtrayati viprān sa śrāddham uddiśya nirghṛṇaḥ
verses.translation: "Disguising in Bhraman's semblance and speaking sophisticatedly that Ilvala used to invite Brahmans for the purpose of obsequial ceremonies, where Brahman are fed after usual ceremony to appeases their manes.
notes: Here the word sam skṛta is another point for discussion for commentators saying that the demon Ilvala used to speak in chaste Sanskrit. This is one version. The other is as above speaking sophisticatedly. But as could be seen all the raakshasa-s are Vedic pundits and thus there is no oddity in their speaking chaste Sanskrit. Hence their luring or sophisticated talk to entice Brahmans is taken valid. The following verse also has the same word, meaning refinement.

verses.devanagari:
भ्रातरम् संस्कृतम् कृत्वा ततः तम् मेष रूपिणम् |
तान् द्विजान् भोजयामास श्राद्ध दृष्टेन कर्मणा
verses.iast:
bhrātaram saṃskṛtam kṛtvā tataḥ tam meṣa rūpiṇam |
tān dvijān bhojayāmāsa śrāddha dṛṣṭena karmaṇā
verses.translation: Then Ilvala used to make his brother Vaataapi into a ram, perfect that ram's meat into deliciously cooked food, and used to feed Brahmans according to obsequial rites and deeds.

glosses.meaning: then, according to obsequial rites, and deeds

verses.devanagari:
ततो भुक्तवताम् तेषाम् विप्राणाम् इल्वलो अब्रवीत् |
वातापे निष्क्रमस्व इति स्वरेण महता वदन्
verses.iast:
tato bhuktavatām teṣām viprāṇām ilvalo abravīt |
vātāpe niṣkramasva iti svareṇa mahatā vadan
verses.translation: "When those Brahmans are surfeited with that ram's meat, then Ilvala used to shout loudly, "oh, Vaataapi, you may come out."

glosses.meaning: oh, Vaataapi, you exit, thus, he said [use to say]

verses.devanagari:
ततो भ्रातुर् वचः श्रुत्वा वातापिः मेषवत् नदन् |
भित्त्वा भित्वा शरीराणि ब्राह्मणानाम् विनिष्पतत्
verses.iast:
tato bhrātur vacaḥ śrutvā vātāpiḥ meṣavat nadan |
bhittvā bhitvā śarīrāṇi brāhmaṇānām viniṣpatat
verses.translation: "Then on listening his brother's words Vaataapi used to lunge out bleating like a ram, tearing and rending the bodies of those Brahmans.

glosses.meaning: then, Vaataapi, brother's, words, on listening

verses.devanagari:
ब्राह्मणानाम् सहस्राणि तैः एवम् काम रूपिभिः |
विनाशितानि संहत्य नित्यशः पिशित अशनैः
verses.iast:
brāhmaṇānām sahasrāṇi taiḥ evam kāma rūpibhiḥ |
vināśitāni saṃhatya nityaśaḥ piśita aśanaiḥ
verses.translation: "This way they the guise changing demons always ruined thousands of Brahmans together, greedy for raw-flesh as they are.
notes: Some say that the wording taiḥ they, is plural ad it is not accommodative, and some ancient text of unknown reference contained these words, tābhyām evam paramtapa piśita aśayā by them two, that way, Lakshmana, for piśita āśayā raw meat, avaricious as they are, they used to kill.

glosses.meaning: raw meat, eaters kaama ruupibhiH = them, thus, guise-changers
this way, are ruined, together, always.

verses.devanagari:
अगस्त्येन तदा देवैः प्रार्थितेन महर्षिणा |
अनुभूय किल श्राद्धे भक्षितः स महा असुरः
verses.iast:
agastyena tadā devaiḥ prārthitena maharṣiṇā |
anubhūya kila śrāddhe bhakṣitaḥ sa mahā asuraḥ
verses.translation: "Then by Sage Agastya, whom gods have prayed to end this demonic menace, and whom demon Ilvala invited to feast during obsequial rites, he that Agastya having relished the fiendish demon in the form of ram, they say, had finished him off.

glosses.meaning: by gods, one who is prayed
that, fiendish demon, is devoured, they say so.

verses.devanagari:
ततः संपन्नम् इति उक्त्वा दत्त्वा हस्ते अवनेजनम् |
भ्रातरम् निष्क्रमस्व इति च इल्वलः समभाषत
verses.iast:
tataḥ sampannam iti uktvā dattvā haste avanejanam |
bhrātaram niṣkramasva iti ca ilvalaḥ samabhāṣata
verses.translation: "Then Ilvala while giving lateral hand wash into the palms of Agastya entered in the routine conversation of obsequies asking, "Is this rite fulfilled..." and he furthered it in calling his brother to come out.

glosses.meaning: whether [ obsequial rites are] fulfilled?, thus, when asked
in palms, lateral, hand-wash, having given

verses.devanagari:

notes: This saying of Agastya has remained as an epigram till date. That demon Ilvala called out, "Vaataapi..." for which Agastya replied jīrṇam 'digested...' and after repeating this exchange for some time, these questions and answers are combined to form this sentence: jīrṇam jīrṇam vātāpi jīrṇam meaning that 'Vaataapi is digested...' It means that mothers wished their babies should digest any indigestible or food ruinous to health, as has been digested by Sage Agastya. It is said Agastya prohibited any kind of meat to Brahmans, as meat food will be shearing their stomachs with it ram's horns from then on. of godly-saint Agastya, in the name of

verses.devanagari:

संदेशम् पालयन् तस्य विंध्य शैलो न वर्धते
अयम् दीर्घ आयुषः तस्य लोके विश्रुत कर्मणः |

sandeśam pālayan tasya viṃdhya śailo na vardhate
ayam dīrgha āyuṣaḥ tasya loke viśruta karmaṇaḥ |
agastyasya āśramaḥ śrīmān vinīta mṛga sevitaḥ
verses.translation: "Complying which sage's directive Mt. Vindhya ceased to heighten in order not to obstruct the path of the sun, such sage's hermitage is this who is renowned in the world by his deeds and whose longevity is inestimable, hence this glorious hermitage is adored by well-behaved animals and humans as well.
notes: The name Agastya is derived from a famous act of this Sage. Mt. Meru is the highest peak on earth. By its nature it grows day by day, and stands first to be saluted by the rising sun in east every day. Jealous of this Mt. Meru, Mt. Vindhya started to rise to exceed the height of Mt. Meru, thus obstructing the sun's path. Then the day changed for night and the travel of Sun and Moon, the performance of Vedic rituals, which are bound by the solar lunar movement, went topsy-turvy. Then the gods prayed Agastya to do something to decrease the height of Mt. Meru. Agastya and his wife then were coming to Mt. Vindhya and seeing its height, he requested Mt. Vindhya, "Oh, Mountain King Vindhya, myself and my wife are going southward, and we are not able to climb this much height... kindly lower yourself, so that we old people climb you and go to the other side..." Mt. Vindhya being an ardent worshipper of sages and saints immediately lowered his height to the ground level, so that the old couple need not climb but just walk over him. Agastya and his wife on coming to the southern side of the mountain again requested Mt. Vindhya to be at this height only, for they will be returning soon to north. Mt. Vindhya readily agreed for that also, and it is lying like that even today. Because Agastya did not return to north on coming to south Mt. Vindhya is still believed to be at ground level. Thus the solar and lunar movement, seasons' revolve, Vedic calendars etc. are again put to normalcy. Thus the name Agastya, aga stha mountain, stopper, agam sthāsyati or, stabhnāti iti agastyaḥ. He played an important role in uplifting southern regions of India, namely Dravidian cultures. Hid wife is Lopaamudra, the saintly lady will be quoted in Lalitha Sahasra Naamaavali. The thousand name of Mother Universe.

verses.devanagari:
आगताः स्म आश्रम पदम् सौमित्रे प्रविश अग्रतः |
निवेदय इह माम् प्राप्तम् ऋषये सह सीतया
verses.iast:
āgatāḥ sma āśrama padam saumitre praviśa agrataḥ |
nivedaya iha mām prāptam ṛṣaye saha sītayā
verses.translation: "We arrived at the threshold of the hermitage, oh, Soumitri, you enter firstly and submit to Sage Agastya about my arrival at this place along with Seetha.
notes: This is an important point of Rama's speaking to Lakshmana for a protocol to enter the hermitage. Earlier all the three used to enter together, releasing bowstrings and in all their submissiveness. But here Rama wants to follow an imperial protocol to announce his arrival there. Rama is said to have asked Lakshmana to inform the sage that karta subject to eliminate -- himself; and the object, or the instrument to eliminate Ravana, namely Seetha have come. Rama says in above verses that he would like to spend rest of the exile here in this hermitage. But Sage Agastya later asks him to proceed to Panchavati, i.e., towards the dominions of demons. For that and for keeping the sage informed about the arrival of time to eradicate Ravana, Rama seeks this protocol.
